lessons.title: Describing nouns with verbs
lessons.explanation: Use ~는 것 to turn a verb phrase into a noun-like expression, such as ‘the act of studying’ or ‘the thing that I like’. This lesson is the foundation for the next several lessons.

cards.translation: I like listening to music.
cards.hint: Use the present-tense verb modifier + 것, then 을.
cards.explanation: 듣다 → 듣는 것; the noun-like phrase is 음악을 듣는 것을.

cards.translation: Studying Korean is difficult.
cards.hint: Use ~는 것 as the subject, followed by 이.
cards.explanation: 공부하다 → 공부하는 것; as the subject, it becomes 공부하는 것이.

cards.translation: Cooking is fun for me.
cards.hint: 하다 becomes 하는 것.
cards.explanation: 요리하는 것이 means ‘cooking’ as the subject of 재미있어요.

cards.translation: Exercising every day is good for your health.
cards.hint: Use ~는 것 as the topic with 은/는.
cards.explanation: 매일 운동하는 것은 sets ‘exercising every day’ as the topic.

cards.translation: Meeting new people is enjoyable.
cards.hint: Meet: 만나다 → 만나는 것.
cards.explanation: 만나다 becomes 만나는 것, then 이 marks the subject.

lessons.title: Past descriptions with ~던/었던 것
lessons.explanation: Use past modifier forms before 것 to describe something that happened in the past or was in progress in the past. Compare these forms with ~은 것.

cards.translation: The movie I watched yesterday was really good.
cards.hint: Use the completed past modifier of 보다.
cards.explanation: 보다 → 본 before a noun.

cards.translation: This is the house where I used to live as a child.
cards.hint: Use ~던 for a past habit or ongoing past situation.
cards.explanation: 살다 → 살던 describes the house connected with a past situation.

cards.translation: I am looking for the book I read last week.
cards.hint: Use the completed past modifier.
cards.explanation: 읽다 → 읽은 책.

cards.translation: It is a café I used to go to often.
cards.hint: Use ~던 for a repeated past action.
cards.explanation: 가다 → 가던 in a remembered/repeated past context.

cards.translation: The food I ate yesterday was spicy.
cards.hint: 먹다 takes the past modifier ~은.
cards.explanation: 먹다 → 먹은 음식.

lessons.title: More uses of ~는 것
lessons.explanation: Build on ~는 것 with irregular verbs, preference expressions, and common noun-like constructions. Pay attention to how the form combines with 이다 and particles.

cards.translation: The thing I like doing most is traveling.
cards.hint: The verb before 것은 is in the present modifier form.
cards.explanation: 좋아하다 → 좋아하는 것; before 은, the ending is 좋아하는 것은.

cards.translation: Learning Korean is interesting.
cards.hint: 배우다 becomes 배우는 before 것.
cards.explanation: 배우는 것이 means ‘learning’ as the subject.

cards.translation: What I dislike is waiting.
cards.hint: Use the present modifier ending before 것은.
cards.explanation: 싫어하다 → 싫어하는 것은.

cards.translation: I like resting on weekends.
cards.hint: Use 쉬는 것.
cards.explanation: 쉬다 → 쉬는 것.

cards.translation: Eating spicy food is difficult.
cards.hint: 먹다 becomes 먹는 before 것.
cards.explanation: 먹는 것이 is the subject phrase ‘eating’.

lessons.title: Nominalizing with ~기 and ~ㅁ/음
lessons.explanation: Use ~기 and ~ㅁ/음 to turn verbs and adjectives into nouns. These forms overlap with ~는 것 but have different common patterns and registers.

cards.translation: Learning Korean is difficult.
cards.hint: Attach 기, then add 가 as the subject particle.
cards.explanation: 배우다 + 기가 → 배우기가 어려워요.

cards.translation: Exercising every day is important.
cards.hint: Use 하다 + 기 + 가.
cards.explanation: 운동하기가 중요해요 means ‘exercising is important’.

cards.translation: I dislike going to bed late.
cards.hint: 자다 + 기, then 가.
cards.explanation: 늦게 자기가 싫어요 is a natural nominalized expression.

cards.translation: I was happy to hear the news.
cards.hint: This sentence uses the result expression after 듣다; focus on the connective form.
cards.explanation: This is a context card linking nominalization with a natural follow-up expression.

cards.translation: Thank you for helping me.
cards.hint: Use the honorific connective form of 주다.
cards.explanation: 도와주셔서 고마워요 is the polite expression used here.

lessons.title: Expressing uncertainty and duration
lessons.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I do not know who that person is.
cards.hint: 이다 becomes 인지 after a noun.
cards.explanation: 누구인지 모르겠어요 means ‘I don’t know who it is’.

cards.translation: I am not sure whether it will rain today.
cards.hint: Use the present form of a verb before 지.
cards.explanation: 오다 → 오는지.

cards.translation: I am not sure whether I will have time tomorrow.
cards.hint: Use the future/possibility form after a consonant.
cards.explanation: 있다 → 있을지.

cards.translation: It has been two years since I came to Korea.
cards.hint: 온 지 + time period expresses duration since an action.
cards.explanation: 온 지 2년 됐어요 means ‘two years have passed since I came’.

cards.translation: Do you know how long it takes?
cards.hint: 걸리다 is a present verb before 지.
cards.explanation: 얼마나 걸리는지 알아요? asks how long something takes.

lessons.title: ~는 것 with 이다
lessons.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

cards.translation: This is something I made.
cards.hint: Use 것 + 이에요 after a noun ending in a consonant.
cards.explanation: 것이에요 is the polite form of ‘is a thing’.

cards.translation: There is something I want to say.
cards.hint: Use 것 as the subject before 있어요.
cards.explanation: 말하고 싶은 것이 있어요 means ‘there is something I want to say’.

cards.translation: It is not that I am studying right now.
cards.hint: Use the present modifier + 것 + 이.
cards.explanation: 공부하는 것이 아니에요 negates the noun-like statement.

cards.translation: This is what I want.
cards.hint: Set the noun-like phrase as the topic.
cards.explanation: 원하는 것은 이거예요 means ‘the thing I want is this’.

cards.translation: I think learning Korean is good.
cards.hint: 배우다 → 배우는 것, then 이.
cards.explanation: 배우는 것이 좋은 것 같아요.

lessons.title: Purpose and trying
lessons.explanation: Use ~려고 and ~러 to express purpose, and ~아/어 보다 to say that you try or experience doing something.

cards.translation: I came to Korea to learn Korean.
cards.hint: Purpose with the same subject uses ~려고.
cards.explanation: 배우려고 한국에 왔어요.

cards.translation: I went to a café to meet a friend.
cards.hint: Use ~러 with a movement verb such as 가다.
cards.explanation: 만나러 카페에 갔어요.

cards.translation: I want to try eating this food.
cards.hint: 먹다 combines with ~어 보다.
cards.explanation: 먹어 보고 싶어요 means ‘want to try eating’.

cards.translation: How about trying a new method?
cards.hint: Use 보다 as a noun-like suggestion.
cards.explanation: 사용해 보는 것은 어때요? is a natural suggestion to try using it.

cards.translation: I booked a flight in order to go to Jeju Island.
cards.hint: Use purpose ~려고 before 예약했어요.
cards.explanation: 가려고 비행기를 예약했어요.

lessons.title: The noun 중
lessons.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: I am doing my homework right now.
cards.hint: Use the present modifier before 중.
cards.explanation: 숙제를 하는 중이에요 means ‘I am in the middle of doing homework’.

cards.translation: I am in a meeting, so I will call later.
cards.hint: Use 중이다 before 라서.
cards.explanation: 회의하는 중이라서 means ‘because I am in a meeting’.

cards.translation: Among my friends, Minsu is the fastest.
cards.hint: Put 중에서 after the group noun.
cards.explanation: 친구들 중에서 means ‘among my friends’.

cards.translation: Choose one among the three options.
cards.hint: Use 중에서 after a noun group.
cards.explanation: 세 가지 중에서 means ‘among three things’.

cards.translation: I am driving right now, so I cannot see messages.
cards.hint: Use 운전하는 중이다.
cards.explanation: 운전하는 중이니까 means ‘because I am in the middle of driving’.
